words.sense: Excessively and weakly sentimental, especially tearful or self-pitying
misconceptions: Any sadness or tears must be maudlin
Intensity alone matters more than how sadness is expressed

words.sense: Deep, sustained sadness without excessive sentimental display
misconceptions: Quiet or lasting sadness is automatically sentimental excess
Intensity alone matters more than how sadness is expressed

semantic_axes.description: Whether the scene turns on sentimental excess.
Whether the scene turns on emotional restraint.

edges.boundary_rule: Maudlin sadness is excessively sentimental or self-pitying; melancholy sadness is deep and lasting without that excess.

misconceptions.M1: Any sadness or tears must be maudlin
misconceptions.M2: Quiet or lasting sadness is automatically sentimental excess
misconceptions.M3: Intensity alone matters more than how sadness is expressed

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mina’s response to the old family photographs?

beats.text: Mina studied the photographs with a sad, distant expression and barely spoke.
beats.reason: The detail about sad and restrained at first supports melancholy more strongly than maudlin.

beats.text: Soon she was sobbing over every snapshot, insisting nobody had ever suffered as much as she had.
beats.reason: The detail about repeated, exaggerated self-pity supports maudlin more strongly than melancholy.

chains.feedback_short: Repeated, exaggerated self-pity makes maudlin the better description.
chains.feedback_deep: Initially, sad and restrained at first points toward melancholy. The new detail, repeated, exaggerated self-pity, instead makes maudlin the stronger choice. Maudlin sadness is excessively sentimental or self-pitying; melancholy sadness is deep and lasting without that excess.

hints.attention: Watch how the sadness is expressed, not just its intensity.
hints.axis: Whether the scene turns on sentimental excess.
